Class JdkInstrumentationInstaller

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.instrumentation.JdkInstrumentationInstaller
public final class JdkInstrumentationInstaller extends Object
Static-only installer that wires ByteBuddy instrumentation for all JDK interception points.

Startup sequence

  1. install(Instrumentation, ChaosRuntime, boolean, List, List, Path) is called once by ChaosAgentBootstrap after the runtime is ready. It first refuses a JVM whose dispatcher already carries the delegate of another copy of the agent, before any step that cannot be undone.
  2. BridgeInjector.injectBridge(java.lang.instrument.Instrumentation, java.nio.file.Path) packages BootstrapDispatcher and the types woven advice references into a temporary JAR and appends it to the bootstrap classpath so that bootstrap-loaded JDK classes can see it.
  3. ModuleOpener.grantInternalModuleOpens(Instrumentation) opens the JDK-internal packages the advice reads.
  4. installDelegate(Object) constructs a ChaosBridge, builds the HANDLE_COUNT-slot MethodHandle array via buildMethodHandles(), and calls the bootstrap-loaded BootstrapDispatcher.install() via reflection to wire the bridge.
  5. ByteBuddy's AgentBuilder is assembled with one transformation per interception point and installed via AgentBuilder.installOn(java.lang.instrument.Instrumentation).

On-demand weaving

Every interception point belongs to a JdkInstrumentationInstaller.HookGroup tagged with the operations it serves. A group is woven the first time a scenario for one of its operations is activated (or, for the executor groups, when a session is opened) and stays woven until uninstall(Instrumentation). A JVM with the agent attached but no scenario carries no advice in its JDK classes. eager weaves every group at install time. The same path serves static attach (-javaagent:), dynamic attach and self-attach: the installer relies on ByteBuddy's RedefinitionStrategy.RETRANSFORMATION combined with disableClassFormatChanges() to rewrite already-loaded JDK classes such as java.net.Socket.

Retransformation

All transformations use disableClassFormatChanges() combined with RedefinitionStrategy.RETRANSFORMATION to allow live retransformation of already-loaded JDK classes without changing the class format.

Thread safety

install(Instrumentation, ChaosRuntime, boolean, List, List, Path) is expected to be called once at startup, from a single thread. weave(Instrumentation, Set) and uninstall(Instrumentation) may run on any thread: the woven groups are guarded by their map's monitor.

  • Method Details

    • install

      public static void install(Instrumentation instrumentation, ChaosRuntime runtime, boolean eager, List<String> clockCallSitePackages, List<String> sessionHeaderHosts, @Nullable Path bridgeDir)
      Installs the agent into the JVM: grants the module opens the advice needs, injects the bootstrap bridge and wires the ChaosBridge delegate to runtime.

      Hooks are woven on demand: the runtime calls back into weave(Instrumentation, Set) before a scenario that needs a hook group starts (and when a session opens, for executor task decoration), so a JVM without scenarios carries no advice in its JDK classes. The same path serves premain, agentmain and self-attach.

      In the classes under clockCallSitePackages, calls to System.currentTimeMillis() and System.nanoTime() are rewritten to go through the clock-skew dispatch once a SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS or SYSTEM_CLOCK_NANOS scenario is activated: the methods are JIT intrinsics no advice can reach, their call sites can be rewritten.

      Parameters:
      instrumentation - the Instrumentation handle provided by the JVM at agent attachment
      runtime - the runtime the bridge dispatches to
      eager - true to weave every hook group immediately instead of on demand, so no activation pays the one-time weaving cost
      clockCallSitePackages - package (or class-name) prefixes whose clock calls are rewritten, e.g. com.example.; java., javax., jdk., sun. and com.sun. prefixes are refused
      sessionHeaderHosts - host globs that receive X-Chaos-Session besides the internal hosts (* for all)
      bridgeDir - the directory for the bootstrap bridge jar (bridgeDir), already checked by the caller; null for java.io.tmpdir, then /dev/shm
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a clock prefix names JDK classes
      IllegalStateException - if the bootstrap class path already holds the bridge of another agent revision, or a copy of the agent loaded by another class loader is installed (nothing is changed then; when that copy installs while this one is installing, only this one's module opens stay), or if a later step fails (the delegate and the hooks are removed again)

    • uninstall

      public static boolean uninstall(Instrumentation instrumentation)
      Resets the installed ByteBuddy transformer, reverting class transformations applied by the most recent install(Instrumentation, ChaosRuntime, boolean, List, List, Path) call.

      Callable by dynamic-attach test runners between suites, or by framework teardown paths that need to detach chaos interception without restarting the JVM. Safe to call when no install has occurred — the no-transformer state is a silent no-op.

      Parameters:
      instrumentation - the same Instrumentation handle originally passed to install(Instrumentation, ChaosRuntime, boolean, List, List, Path); required so the underlying JVMTI retransformation can see the previously transformed classes

      Every step runs even when an earlier one fails: the delegate is cleared, the transformers are removed and the hook coverage is reset, so a later install starts empty.

      Returns:
      true if a transformer was reset or this copy's delegate was cleared; false if there was nothing to undo
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - after every step ran, if the JVM refused to retransform a class back (it keeps the advice) or another step failed: the first failure, with the later ones attached as suppressed

    • connectDispatcher

      @Internal public static AutoCloseable connectDispatcher(ChaosRuntime runtime) throws Exception
      Connects runtime to the BootstrapDispatcher without weaving any class, so benchmarks and tests can drive the dispatch methods exactly as woven advice does. Closing the result disconnects it again, unless another delegate replaced it in the meantime.

      For benchmarks and tests on the plain (thin) chaos-agent-instrumentation-jdk classes only: it installs into the dispatcher this class links against, which is the bootstrap copy only when no agent jar injected one. The agent jar keeps the dispatcher out of its own loader's view (META-INF/macstab-chaos-bridge/), so there it resolves only once install(Instrumentation, ChaosRuntime, boolean, List, List, Path) injected the bridge.

      Parameters:
      runtime - the runtime that receives the dispatches
      Returns:
      a handle that uninstalls this delegate when closed
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if a copy of the agent loaded by another class loader is installed
      Exception - if the method handles cannot be built
